newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Suncor wins okay for Australia venture.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Suncor wins okay for Australia venture.

text.p: Canada's Suncor Inc has won Australian foreign investment approval to join the Stuart Energy Joint Venture, formed to develop the Stuart oil shale deposit in Queensland, the Australian partners said on Monday.
Suncor will hold a 50 percent interest, with the two Australian partners, the so-called "Rundle Twins" -- Southern Pacific Petroleum NL and Central Pacific Minerals NL -- each holding 25 percent.
Suncor also won approval to acquire share interests in Southern Pacific and Central Pacific under terms approved by shareholders of the two companies last month, they said.
The terms give Suncor about 22 percent interests in both companies, excluding their cross shareholdings, the companies said.

The issues of Restricted Class Shares to Suncor and Suncor's participation in the project will be subject to the financial close of the first of three stages of the project, located near Gladstone, the companies said.
The partners are proposing to construct a pilot plant to produce 4,500 barrels of oil a day.
Pending successful operation of the first stage, subsequent stages could raise production progressively to a total of 85,000 barrels a day, with the prospect of additional production, the twins said.
A work programme is under way over engineering and funding for the project, the companies said.
Suncor has said it will spend about A$7 million to conduct preliminary engineering work on the project.
